Non-convex optimization problems pervade machine learning, from neural network training to
matrix factorization and tensor decomposition. A fundamental challenge in these problems is
the presence of saddle points—stationary points where the Hessian has negative eigenvalues.

the presence of saddle points—stationary points where the Hessian has negative eigenvalues. While gradient descent can efficiently decrease the function value when the gradient is large, it
can stagnate near saddle points where the gradient is small but the Hessian indicates negative
curvature [9, 11].
